item.title: Just a lot of stuff about payments
item.description:
Ledgers

  • For broadly scoped payments systems, ledgers (basically double entry book keeping) will often be source of truth in your system. 10/10 IMHO.
  • It’s a really a good way to get into thinking of how accounting and accountants work.
  • Good resources
    • https://www.moderntreasury.com/journal/accounting-for-developers-part-i
    • https://www.moderntreasury.com/journal/accounting-for-developers-part-ii
    • https://www.moderntreasury.com/journal/accounting-for-developers-part-iii
    • https://martin.kleppmann.com/2011/03/07/accounting-for-computer-scientists.html

Safety

  • Be very paranoid when building payments systems

Reconciliation

  • Reconciliation at a high level to me is verifying data (at aggregate or txn level) against other systems or reality you interact with.
  • Especially important when settlement is not instant and feedback loop is delayed.
  • Good philosophy is start from being paranoid and not believing transaction data in your database blindly. Reconciliations gives you confidence to trust your data.
  • Inherently involves operational muscle in org. Needs someone to be responsible and reconcile every week. Ideally that person automates some parts of the recon but does spot checks as well
  • interesting reads
    • https://stripe.com/in/resources/more/accounting-reconciliation-101#types-of-accounting-reconciliation
    • https://stripe.com/in/resources/more/payment-reconciliation-101

item.title: Work Beliefs
item.description:
• autonomy
    • take personal responsibility to be proactive and be the owner of implementation E2E
  • craftsmanship
    • never half-ass anything that ships
    • details and elegance matter for designing/building/operating solid systems
  • curiosity
    • best work is not defined but discovered under constraints and in context
  • deep dive
    • get to the root of problem and fix that
    • aim to better understand wider systems
  • pragmatic
    • strong ownership, but value stakeholder input
    • high level sense of urgency, but not hurried
    • some details matter than other - no bike shedding
    • know when to dive deep. weigh practise over academicy-ivory-tower theory
